items.summary: Add `routing.clientPromptParity` (`taksim routing prompt-parity on|off|status`, off by default;).
items.details: With it on, when `taksim claude` may serve a session with a model other than its start model, it disables the start model's Claude Code prompt bundle (initially `opus_5_5_prompt_bundle` for Opus 5.5) through the undocumented `CLAUDE_CODE_MODEL_CAPABILITIES` variable. Only for Claude Code versions verified to read it (2.1.306); any other or unknown version sets nothing and records a bounded reason in `TAKSIM_CLIENT_PROMPT_PARITY`. Managed or remote Claude settings outrank Taksim, so a value from them is left alone (`managed-override`). When the setting is on but nothing is applied (`version-unverified`, `version-unknown`, `managed-override`), `taksim claude` prints one line at launch and `taksim routing prompt-parity status` shows why. The user's own value is merged, never replaced and never printed. Dated model ids (`claude-opus-5-5-2026...`) and an `ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL` behind the `opus` alias are resolved first. The `claude --version` probe is cached per executable path, last-write time and size. Sessions that stay on Opus also lose the Opus bundle; the effect on Opus quality is unmeasured.

items.summary: An escalation backed by evidence that the model was not enough (failed verification, repair, repeated invalid tool input, a blocking finding) now sticks for its phase.
items.details: Before, an escalation that leased Opus 5.5 without an explicit effort lasted one call: the next main-conversation request asked for its own effort, the keep-current check failed on the effort, and Opus 5.5 carries no escalation role, so nothing kept the lease. Such a lease is now marked `QUALITY_ESCALATION_LEASE` and kept (`ESCALATION_LEASE_STICKY`), at the request's explicit effort when it gives one.

items.summary: A prompt-only escalation (complexity, qualified risk) no longer moves the session's lease.
items.details: In SWE-bench Pro held-out runs every mid-session escalation came from a small side request, which closed the main conversation's Sonnet lease; the next main call then dropped back to Sonnet. Such an escalation now serves that one request on the escalated model (`PROMPT_ESCALATION_SINGLE_REQUEST`), takes no lease and leaves the context's lease and warm cache in place.

items.summary: A step down within a phase is now quoted instead of always refused.
items.details: The gateway keeps the provider usage of each session's last 32 calls in memory and compares the cost of rewriting the prefix on the cheaper model (largest recent prefix x the target's cache-write rate for the TTL in use) with the per-token saving on the session's mean output and uncached input over at most 10 further calls. It steps down only when the saving beats the switch cost by 1.5x and the lease has served 3 calls (`SWITCH_COST_QUOTED_DOWNGRADE`); otherwise it keeps the model (`SWITCH_COST_EXCEEDS_SAVING_KEEP_CURRENT`, `SWITCH_COST_STEP_DOWN_COOLDOWN`, or `SWITCH_COST_UNKNOWN_KEEP_CURRENT` without usage). Escalations, pins, budget fallbacks and the downgrade-escalation latch never consult the quote. See Cache-aware stickiness.

items.summary: Switch-cost routing after review.
items.details: Stickiness keys on the lease's escalated-to state, not on the model's catalog role, and a latched downgrade escalation is sticky without a quote, so it no longer proposes the cheaper model for the latch to override on every call. A prompt-only escalation serves a single request only for a small side context (below half of the session's largest recent prefix, or below 20k tokens without usage); in the main conversation it takes an ordinary lease that the quote may step down. An explicit effort change renews the lease on the same model with its start, call count and markers kept (`LEASE_EFFORT_RENEWAL`), so a first-request escalation at `medium` no longer drops to Sonnet on the next request's `high`, and the cooldown no longer restarts. Cold-start keeps (security flag, learned keep) are never stepped down by the quote. An evidence escalation waits 10 calls before a step down is quoted. The saving uses the lease's own calls, a target that is not cheaper reports `SWITCH_COST_NOT_CHEAPER`, only canonical calls feed the usage ledger, and the ledger evicts the least recently observed session in constant time. The renewal also keeps the auto-default and budget-downgrade markers, which it had dropped.

items.summary: Failed test runs that no hook reports now count for downgrade escalation.
items.details: The gateway reads the previous turn's tool results in each Claude request: a test or build command whose result is an error starting with `Exit code 1`-`123`, or that exited 0 (`| tail`, `|| true`) while its output carries a test runner's own failure summary (Jest, Vitest, Mocha, `go test`, pytest, `dotnet test`, `cargo test`, Maven Surefire), is one failed run. It feeds the same counter, two-failure threshold and guards as `PostToolUseFailure` hooks, and a run seen in both counts once (keyed by its `tool_use_id`). Before, a stepped-down session whose failure hooks were lost or never fired stayed on the cheaper model: in one SWE-bench Pro run, six test runs reached Taksim as zero failures. Only the start and end of each result are read, and only a hash of each failed run's id is kept, in memory. An escalation that used this evidence carries `DOWNGRADE_ESCALATION_EVIDENCE_TOOL_RESULT`. See Failed runs in the request body.

items.summary: Only failed fix attempts count, not reproductions, from hooks and request bodies alike.
items.details: A failed test run counts toward downgrade escalation only when the session edited a non-test source file since its previous test run (or since session start). A run that reproduces the bug before any edit, or a TDD red run after test-only edits, is a red baseline and is not counted, so an agent that checks the failure first no longer escalates on that alone. Edits come from `Edit`, `Write`, `MultiEdit` and `NotebookEdit` calls in the request bodies and their `PostToolUse` hooks, deduplicated by `tool_use_id`. A file is a test file by path shape only (`test`/`tests`/`__tests__`/`spec` directories, `*_test.go`, `*.test.*`, `*.spec.*`, `test_*.py`, `*_test.py`, `*Tests.cs`). A fix attempt whose runner summary shows fewer failed tests than the previous failed run is progress and does not count. The two-failure threshold and every guard are unchanged. Only a flag, the last failed count and counters are kept per session, in memory; no path is stored. See Reproductions do not count.

items.summary: Fix-attempt evidence after review.
items.details: Only a real runner invocation (a runner as a command word) is a run: `cat`, `grep`, `rg`, `git`, `ls`, `head`, `tail`, `echo`, `sed -n` and `find` are never runs, their output is never read, and they no longer reset "source edited since the last run". A bare `AssertionError` line is no longer a failure marker (passing `pytest -s` runs print them). A successful shell command that may write files (`sed -i`, `perl -i`, a redirection, a heredoc, `tee`, `patch`, `cp`, `mv`, `git apply`, `git checkout -- <path>`) counts as a source edit, except a redirect to a `.log`, `.txt` or `.out` file, a temp directory or `/dev/`, a `cat <<EOF` heredoc with no write redirect, and `cp`, `mv`, `tee` or `patch` with every target in a temp directory (`go vet ./... 2> vet.log` is not a fix attempt). A hook's edited path is classified relative to its `cwd`, otherwise by its last three segments, so a `test` directory above the project no longer makes every edit a test edit; `*.Tests`/`*.Test` directories and `*Test.cs`, `*Test.java` and `*_spec.rb` files are test files. Fewer failures is progress only for the same command (a short hash, in memory) and at most twice in a row before a pass. An unkeyed hook failure keeps body evidence out only for its failure window; an unkeyed edit or pass no longer switches body evidence off for the session. Hooks and bodies use one predicate: a runner that exited 1-123 or a runner failure summary on exit 0.

items.summary: Failing test runs now escalate a stepped-down session.
items.details: A test or build command that exits with status 1-123 is labelled a failed verification command before its output is searched for environment or permission words. Before, a failing `go test` or `jest` run whose output contained "timeout", "network", "denied", "unauthorized" or just a `0.429s` duration was labelled an environment failure, so it never reached the two-failure threshold of downgrade escalation, and an Opus start stepped down to Sonnet stayed on Sonnet through repeated failing runs. Exit codes 124-127 (timeout, could not start, not found) keep their old labels.

items.summary: A test or build runner now counts only as a command word, at the start of a command or after `;`, `&&`, `||`, `|`, `(`, `cd X &&`, environment assignments or a wrapper.
items.details: Before, any command containing `tsc`, `jest`, `pytest`, `make `, `mvn ` or `gradle` counted, so `cat tsconfig.json`, `rg jest`, `cmake --version` or a commit message mentioning "make" were taken for test runs. `python -m unittest`, `bun test`, `node --test` and `npx playwright test` are now recognised. `yarn test:unit`, `pnpm test:ci`, `bun build:prod`, `pnpm -r test` and `pnpm --filter web test` count (a script starting `test` or `build`, after leading flags and their values); `command -v pytest` is a lookup and does not.

items.summary: Fix: `routing.max_frontier_share` now counts Opus 5.5.
items.details: Before, only the one catalog resource with the escalation role (Opus 5) counted as frontier, but the ranked policy escalates to Opus 5.5. Opus 5.5 usage therefore never moved the frontier share, and the cap never blocked an Opus 5.5 request. The Claude Code catalog now marks every Opus and Fable model as frontier, and the budget share, budget reservations and recorded usage all use that flag. Resources saved before this change have no flag, so the share derives it from the model id and counts Opus 5.5 right after the upgrade. A month with Haiku traffic no longer reports the frontier share as unknown, which also had switched the cap off. Opus 5 stays the single escalation target, and escalation-lease behaviour is unchanged. The cap now waits for 10 tasks in the month before it applies, so the first request of a month is not a 1/1 share that always hits the cap. **Behaviour change.** If you set `routing.max_frontier_share`, the cap is now enforced where it was not before: Opus 5.5 counts toward it, and Haiku traffic no longer switches it off. A request that would push the share to the cap or above can now end with `MAX_FRONTIER_SHARE_REACHED` and need approval where it ran freely until now. Raise or remove the setting if you want the old behaviour.

items.summary: Blind cross-session judge, so Taksim can learn with only the in-session judge.
items.details: Before, a turn counted only when two different judges agreed, and in most setups the in-session judge was the only strong one, so almost every verdict stayed "single-judge" and nothing learned from it. Now a second Claude model grades such turns blind: the user prompt and the final reply as quoted data under a fresh alias, redacted like a support bundle (absolute paths too), then cut to 3000 characters each, with no model, no earlier grade, no request id and no path. Its verdict is stored as `claude_code_cross_session`, a strong judge, so an agreeing pair is consensus under the existing rule and `routing auto`, policy suggestions, `routing recommend` and the proof counterfactual gain evidence. Only Claude-served turns whose one strong verdict is an in-session verdict at the current prompt version qualify; weak judges do not count against a turn.

items.summary: `taksim judge cross-check export --count N (--project <alias> | --all-projects)` writes such a batch over history, with `--seed` for a reproducible sample, `--since` for the age (default 30 days, at most 90) and `--exclude-session` (default: the managed session it runs in) to leave out a grading session's own turns, forks and anything it was already shown.
items.details: Grade the batch in a fresh `claude -p` run without tools, MCP servers, settings or hooks (the command line is in the docs), then run `taksim judge cross-check submit --grader-model <model> --stdin`: it stores the verdicts only for aliases an export issued in the last 48 h, refuses a Haiku or unknown grader, and prints accepted and rejected counts.

items.summary: The in-session Stop hook also adds one turn per pass that is due anyway (`judge/cross.json` `{"perPass": n}`, or `TAKSIM_JUDGE_CROSS_SESSION_PER_PASS`; at most 2, 0 turns it off) from another session of the same project, never another project, only in `default` permission mode, only while the session runs on Sonnet, Opus or Fable, and only with at least 3 s of the hook deadline left.
items.details: `judge submit` stores a cross verdict only for an alias issued to that session in the last 2 h, and says how many ids it rejected. Issued aliases and `judge backlog` excerpts are kept in `judge/cross-issued.json` (ids and times only, 90 days); the database schema does not change. A corrupt file is set aside and pauses cross turns until a fresh one exists, while submits still record the session's own verdicts.

items.summary: Calibration: `taksim judge status` prints a `Cross-check:` line with the turns issued and graded and how often the in-session judge and the cross judge name the same tier (exact, within one tier, and Cohen's kappa).
items.details: From 50 pairs at 80% exact agreement and a kappa of 0.6 the in-session judge counts as calibrated: its lone verdicts at confidence 0.8 or higher then show as `CALIBRATED_SINGLE_JUDGE` in `insights advisor` and `insights default-model`, and the proof export uses them for the upper bound of its counterfactual (`counterfactual.upperBound`, consensus stays the lower bound) and reports the measurement in `judge.calibration` (schema minor 2, new caveat `SINGLE_JUDGE_UNCALIBRATED`). Routing never reads the calibrated tier. See Blind cross-session check.

items.summary: Launcher watchdog: while a managed session runs, its launcher reads the shared gateway's `/health` every 2 s, and after two misses in a row restarts a gateway that crashed, on the same port and through the same `gateway.lock` path as `gateway ensure`, so two launchers that notice the same crash start one gateway.
items.details: A gateway whose record is gone was stopped on purpose (`gateway stop`, the idle timeout) and stays stopped. A `gateway.failed` marker blocks the restart, and a launcher restarts at most three times in ten minutes; when it cannot restart the gateway it prints one stderr line, `Taksim gateway stopped and could not restart; /exit and run claude directly.` (`codex` and so on for the other launchers), and stops watching. The restarted gateway starts without the old one's in-flight work: a response that was streaming when the gateway died is lost and that one request fails. Every launcher registers its session's lease on the new gateway, also when another launcher restarted it. The gateway no longer logs the per-request lines of its own `/health` reads (or any request) at information level.

items.summary: `taksim gateway stop --force` is refused while a launcher holds a live session lease on the gateway (exit code 3, with the session count); `--force-sessions` stops it anyway.
items.details: Without `--force` it already stopped only an idle gateway, and the `taksim update` hand-off keeps doing that. See Configuration.

items.summary: Offline licence seam (plans: Free, Pro, Team).
items.details: `taksim license activate <file|base64>` verifies an Ed25519-signed licence on this machine (no network call), checks it against public keys compiled into the binary and installs it atomically as `$TAKSIM_HOME/license.json`; `taksim license status [--json]` shows the plan in force, org, seats, expiry, the 14-day grace period, whether licensing is enforced and a feature table; `taksim license deactivate` removes it, `uninstall --purge-data` deletes it with the rest of the home's data and `taksim home migrate` moves it. `taksim doctor` has a `license` block and the status line shows `Taksim Pro` once a licence is installed. A Team licence needs at least 5 seats; a tampered licence grants no plan, with the reason `signature invalid`. Free is everything that saves money or shows evidence (ledger, imports, dashboard, reports, judge, insights, proof export, `taksim mode`, `routing.auto`, subscription routing); Pro ($12 per month) adds `budget enforce`, scheduled digest delivery, the HTML summary export, native-router audit details and priority support; Team ($18 per developer, 5-developer minimum) adds the team roll-up, team budgets and organisation policy. Nothing changes for any user today: paid plans are not on sale yet, licensing is not enforced (the compiled enforcement date is null and the compiled public key is a named placeholder, so no licence verifies in this build), every user is in the founding preview, and `license status` says so. Once enforced, only `budget enforce` consults the plan: without Pro it stores the setting, prints one line naming the plan, and the gateway forwards requests unchanged; nothing ever blocks or fails a Claude request. New `tools/Taksim.LicenseIssuer` (offline `keygen` and `issue`; the private key is never in the repository, `*.key` is git-ignored). See Licensing. EULA section 2 names the Pro features.

items.summary: `taksim diagnostics bundle [--out file.zip]`: writes a redacted zip to attach to a support request.
items.details: It lists the files before it writes them. It holds a header (Taksim version and commit, OS and architecture, build, .NET runtime and `claude --version`), the `taksim doctor` result, the gateway and update status, the hook install state, the settings integrity verdict (not the contents of `settings.json`, whose `env` block can hold credentials), the last fail-open record and the last 500 lines of the gateway log. Your home folder, `TAKSIM_HOME` and account name become `<HOME>`, `<TAKSIM_HOME>` and `<USER>`; API keys, bearer and basic tokens, authorization and cookie headers, secret-named settings, the values of secret-named environment variables and of the `settings.json` `env` block, e-mail addresses and private keys are removed from every file. It never contains prompts, database files or credentials, and never overwrites an existing file. See Configuration.

items.summary: `taksim update --rollback`: switches a release installation back to the previously installed version without a download.
items.details: It checks that the previous version is installed and starts, swaps `current` the way `install-release.ps1` does (a `current.new` link, then a rename; a symlink on macOS), stops an idle gateway of the newer version (or restarts the desktop gateway) and records the rolled-back release in `update-skip.json`, so the update check does not offer it again until a newer release exists (builds from before this change do not read that file). A `current` link that points nowhere, a leftover `current.new` or a plain folder named `current` is repaired on the way and reported (`Fixed: ...`). It refuses when the previous version knows an older database migration than the one your database already has, because an older Taksim on a newer schema can misread it. See Configuration.

items.summary: Start-up: the launcher's own time is now measured, and a cold `taksim claude` launch adds a median 1.75 s (3.27 s for the same source without ReadyToRun) and a warm one 1.05 s (2.13 s).
items.details: The `origin/main` launcher could not be timed on the measuring machine (see the readiness item below), so there is no launcher before/after against the previous release.
points: Schema stamp: after a successful migration the database records the migration count in `PRAGMA user_version`. A start that finds the current count, WAL mode and this build's latest migration in the history skips Entity Framework entirely (no `DbContext`, no pending-migration query), for the launcher, the gateway and the hooks alike. Anything else, including a lower, missing or higher stamp, takes the full migration path, which stays the only writer of the stamp. The gateway's database phase drops from a median 778 ms on main to 82 ms (44 ms with ReadyToRun as well).

The release publish is ReadyToRun (a property of `Taksim.Edge.csproj`, so every workflow and `Build-LocalRelease.ps1` get it). The single-file executable grows from 126.9 MB to 189.5 MB (49.4%). Gateway process start to listening: 1,616 ms on main, 665 ms now.

The launcher's readiness polling of a recorded or just-started gateway confirms a port the OS listener table does not show with a 150 ms loopback connect (the same single connect as the 300 ms confirmation above, shorter because the poll retries). The table can lag a real listener by seconds or more, which kept launches waiting for the full 20 s and then native.

Trace: each managed launch appends one content-free line (phase timings, `reused` or `started`, version, client type) to `gateway/launch-timings.ndjson` (last 50); `TAKSIM_STARTUP_TRACE=1` also prints it to stderr. The gateway records when each managed session first sent `SessionStart` and its first `/v1/messages` (`gateway/session-contacts.ndjson`), and its own database, services and listening times (`gateway/startup.json`). `taksim doctor` shows the last cold and warm launch.

`scripts/Test-ClaudePerformance.ps1 -Client stub` measures all of this with a $0 stand-in for Claude Code and a fake upstream: 30 interleaved rounds per arm, medians on this machine (a shared one, so relative): cold launch added time 1.75 s p50 and 2.18 s p95, warm 1.05 s p50 and 1.29 s p95; without ReadyToRun 3.27 s and 2.13 s. Warm is still above the 400 ms goal: the launcher's session metadata write (about 550 ms) is the next cost to remove. See PERFORMANCE.md.

items.summary: Taksim routes Claude only.
items.details: A Codex request, with an API key or a ChatGPT sign-in, and a Gemini API-key request are now forwarded unchanged, byte for byte (no model or `reasoning.effort` rewrite, whatever the routing mode) and only observed for usage and cost. The `gpt-*` resources stay in the catalog for pricing and observation but are never routing candidates, and the gateway refuses to select any resource whose provider is not Anthropic: such a selection is treated as a routing error and the original request is forwarded. `taksim codex` sessions keep working and keep their usage and cost reporting; they just are not switched between models. README "What is routed" and Routing now say "Codex: observed, not routed".

items.summary: Jev is off the request path.
items.details: The gateway no longer waits for the Jev router before forwarding a request and never applies its choice: when `taksim set-router jev` is on, a prompt excerpt (up to 4,000 characters, unchanged) is sent to TypeSafe only after the provider response was delivered, on the bounded post-response shadow-planning lifetime, for Claude API-key requests whose provider call succeeded, and the choice is discarded after accounting (the call stays a separate service call and counts under `liveRouter` in `/health`). A slow Jev endpoint can no longer delay a request. `routing/jev.json` is read through a 5 second cache instead of once per request. Execution records written earlier that name `decision_engine_pre_request` are left as they are; new records carry `applied: false`.

items.summary: Upstream base URL overrides (`TAKSIM_ANTHROPIC_UPSTREAM_BASE_URL`, `TAKSIM_OPENAI_UPSTREAM_BASE_URL`, `TAKSIM_GEMINI_UPSTREAM_BASE_URL`) must be `https`, or `http` only for a loopback host (`127.0.0.1`, `localhost`, `[::1]`); anything else stops the gateway from starting with `must be HTTPS; HTTP is allowed only for loopback`, so API keys and prompts cannot be sent in the clear to a remote host by a stray environment variable.
The message shown when subscription traffic reaches the gateway no longer tells you to relaunch with `taksim codex` or `taksim devin`.
`taksim proof export` no longer refuses to write on a real home.
items.details: The privacy check treated every word of a recorded repository path as private, so a folder such as `hubui-app-itr-2026` made the bare number `2026` a private term that matched every date in the bundle (exit 3, "would contain a private term"). A part that is only digits, shorter than four characters, a generic path word (`users`, `workspace`, `documents`, `src`, ...) or a word of the bundle's own text is no longer a term on its own. The whole folder name and path, its distinctive parts (`hubui`), user names, machine names, repository IDs and developer aliases still block the export.

items.summary: Gateway start no longer fails when Windows reports an incomplete TCP listener table.
items.details: After some Windows updates and driver changes the listener table (`GetActiveTcpListeners`, `netstat`) omits real listeners, so a healthy gateway was never accepted: `taksim gateway ensure` waited 20 s, logged "did not become ready" and continued natively, and later launches hit the failure backoff. Taksim now uses the table only as a fast positive hint and confirms a negative answer with a short (300 ms) real connect to 127.0.0.1 before concluding that nothing listens. A port that accepts connections but whose owner the table cannot name is reported as held by an unidentified process and is never killed or replaced.

items.summary: First-run value: `taksim doctor`, `taksim setup`, the dashboard Overview and `taksim judge status` say what to do next.
points: `taksim doctor` now prints grouped PASS/WARN/FAIL lines (Install, Database, Clients detected, Credential mode, Gateway, Startup, Hooks, Pricing coverage, Update) and ends with a Plan of at most three next commands. The previous JSON report moved behind `taksim doctor --json`, with the same schema. The probes run side by side, and doctor no longer loads every execution or walks every Claude transcript to build its numbers (about 17 to 19 s before and 5 to 8 s after on a 65,000-execution home, measured with the unoptimised build on a busy machine; judge providers are also probed concurrently).

With `claude` on PATH, doctor classifies the credential mode itself: the cached `claude auth status` answer, or one probe of at most 3 seconds, so a saved `/login` is no longer reported as `unknown`. If it is still unknown (no `claude` on PATH, or the probe did not answer in time, which is no longer read as a subscription), doctor warns and names `taksim doctor --probe-claude-auth`, which keeps the full probe timeout. A timed-out probe in `taksim setup` or the dashboard card likewise falls back to the budget step instead of suggesting subscription routing.
A missing `policy.yaml` is informational in doctor (the JSON `policyStatus` still reads `POLICY_FILE_MISSING`), and doctor stops recommending `taksim history import` once imported turns exist.

`taksim setup` ends with a headline computed from the imported history, `Last 30 days: $X API-equivalent across N sessions; Opus/Fable was P% of it. Upper bound if every Opus/Fable turn had run on Sonnet: $D less ($Y in total). Judges agreed on $a-$b of avoidable spend so far (n turns). In our pilot, routing cost about the same as always-Sonnet.`, then exactly one next command by Claude credential mode: `taksim mode economy` for an API key, `taksim routing subscription on` (with a pointer to the plan-terms note) for a subscription, otherwise `taksim budget set` with a monthly cap 20 percent above the last 30 days. $Y reprices every Opus/Fable-class Claude turn at Sonnet 5 list prices (it never raises the figure), and $D = $X - $Y is the saving that implies, labelled an upper bound: it says nothing about whether Sonnet would have been good enough. `$a-$b` and `n` (the over-served turns counted) come from the digest's downgrade-safe counterfactual (consensus-only), the same one `taksim digest --since 30d` and `taksim proof export` report, so they agree on the judged low, high and turn count (proof export counts whole UTC days, so a turn on the oldest day can land on one side only). With fewer than 20 consensus-judged turns the sentence reads `Judged evidence: not enough judged turns yet (k).`, k being that consensus count. `--json` carries `headline`, `nextStep`, `opusSharePct`, `judgedRangeUsd` (`low`, `high`) and `judgedTurns` (n); `/api/first-run` carries the same fields. The previous four-command list (and its Cursor extras) is gone. The dashboard Overview shows the same card at the top (`/api/first-run`), loaded after the overview so a slow probe never holds it back.

`taksim judge status` hides clients and populations with no turns (no more `0 of 0` lines) unless `--all`, adds one sentence after the coverage lines on what to do, and shows the verdicts per prompt version, including the legacy ones, only with `--verbose`. `--json` is unchanged.

items.summary: `taksim proof export [--since 30d] [--out <path>] [--format json|md]`: a versioned, redacted, hash-stamped bundle of what the local data shows, meant to be published on purpose.
items.details: It reports, over whole UTC days and the previous window of equal length, spend (API-equivalent total, by model family and by credential kind, with `quota-equivalent` marking dollars that are not invoiced), the output-token model mix, routing settings and the live-routed and observed-unrouted cost (kept separate, never added to the counterfactual), judge evidence (strong and weak consensus, disputed and single-judge turns, the requested-versus-sufficient confusion matrix), a strong-consensus-only counterfactual range with N, the cache hit ratio, the main levers (cache breaks, idle gaps, context above 200k, failure loops, spend-spike days), gateway overhead (`not measured` without samples, never zero) and machine-readable caveat codes. It holds counts, dollars and a fixed vocabulary only: no repository aliases or paths, PR or ticket keys, session or request IDs, user or host names, model IDs or times finer than a day, and a privacy check refuses to write a bundle that would contain any. The JSON is canonical (sorted keys, no whitespace) and carries a `sha256` of itself without that field; two exports of the same data in the same window are byte-identical. `--format md` renders a readable receipt that spells out every caveat and the small-window re-identification risk. Nothing is sent anywhere. See Proof export.

items.summary: Prompt-cache hit ratio: `taksim insights cache`, `taksim digest`, `taksim report weekly` and the proof bundle now compute it with one definition, `cache read / (cache read + cache write + uncached input)`, token-weighted over every Claude execution in a session with all three counts recorded (side calls and subagent turns included).
items.details: The same window used to show two different numbers (for example 97.4% against 96.6%) because `insights cache` left side calls and subagent turns out and counted other clients' turns, and the digest counted executions without a session. Existing reports can move by a point or two: the `insights cache` headline is now Claude-only (its per-repository and per-model rows still cover every client), the digest ignores executions that belong to no session, and `insights cache` shows the number of executions behind the ratio (`hitRatioExecutions` in `--json`).

items.summary: Removed local repository paths from the database.
items.details: A repository is now stored as its salted alias only: `source-control discover` (and so `repo discover`, `routing promote` and `policy explain`) no longer writes `repositories.local_root`, a migration sets every existing value to NULL (the column stays, always empty, until a later release drops it), and the places that read it resolve the root from the working directory instead. Spend budgets scoped to a repo still match the current repo through its alias, including from a subdirectory, a linked worktree or a working directory spelled in another case than the disk stores. `report cost --by repo`, `routing recommend` and the dashboard show the alias unless you set a label with `taksim repo alias --name` (the folder-name fallback is gone). The Crush import and judge find a project-local `.crush` only in the repository they run in or through Crush's `projects.json`, no longer in every repository you ever discovered. `logs/gateway.log` writes your user profile folder (on Windows also its 8.3 short name) as `~`. The "no local paths" statement in `docs/PRIVACY_AND_COMPLIANCE.md` now holds.

items.summary: Removed repository branch names from the database.
items.details: `source-control discover` no longer writes `repositories.default_branch` (neither the checked-out branch nor GitHub's default branch), a migration sets every existing value to NULL and zeroes the freed bytes (the column stays, always empty, until a later release drops it), and nothing read the value, so the branch is resolved from the checkout or GitHub at the moment it is needed. The statement in `docs/PRIVACY_AND_COMPLIANCE.md` that the database keeps no branch names now holds.

items.summary: Native-router audits: `taksim insights advisor [--since 7d]` and `taksim insights default-model [--since 7d]`, audits of what Claude's own routing does when Taksim is not choosing.
items.details: `insights advisor` joins the advisor executions recorded since 0.3.17 with the judge verdicts on the same turn and reports advisor cost, the share of advisor calls where the judges say advice was needed (the judge's minimum sufficient tier is above the tier that served the turn), cost by executor/advisor family pair and N. `insights default-model` finds Opus main-thread turns and says who chose Opus: an explicit choice (a user pin at the gateway or an earlier `/model` switch), Taksim-routed, default (a managed gateway request with no pin), or `could not tell`. Claude Code transcripts carry no default-model marker, so imported history alone is `could not tell` and is never guessed. It reports the Opus-default cost and the share of those turns the judges say Sonnet would have sufficed. Every line that holds a share names its evidence tier: `CONSENSUS` (the existing rule) or the new, clearly weaker `PROVISIONAL_SINGLE_JUDGE`, one verdict from a strong Claude judge (the in-session judge, or the API judge on Sonnet or Opus) at confidence 0.8 or higher on a turn without consensus. A share needs 20 judged turns per scope and tier; below that the output says `not enough evidence` with N and no percentage. Weak judges (Jev, small Ollama models) are never counted as provisional evidence, and provisional findings are shown, never applied: `routing auto`, `routing recommend` and policy suggestions still read consensus only. A second strong verdict that disagrees (a human, `codex_in_session` or the Haiku API judge) leaves the turn uncounted. Both audits add one line to `report weekly`, a "Native-router audits" section to `taksim digest` (`nativeRouterAudits` in its JSON) and an aggregate `advisor` and `defaultModel` section to `taksim proof export` (schema minor 1, `schemaMinor`; new caveat codes `ADVISOR_NOT_RECORDED`, `DEFAULT_MODEL_COULD_NOT_TELL` and `PROVISIONAL_SINGLE_JUDGE_SHOWN`). See Native-router audits.

items.summary: `taksim copilot usage` prints an observe-only "Copilot auto model" row: the calls the Copilot SDK flagged `isAuto`, the models it reported serving them and any Fusion attribution, with N.
items.details: It is what Copilot reported, not a Taksim choice; Taksim does not route Copilot. The history importer captures no routed model for Auto or HydraFusion (the usage event holds only that word), so the row comes from the native observation files only.

items.summary: `taksim mode economy|balanced|quality`: one switch over settings that already exist, and `taksim mode` with no argument shows the mode in force, what it maps to and any setting changed by hand since.
items.details: `balanced` is today's defaults. `economy` turns `routing.auto` on and lowers the managed baseline's standard capability demand from 0.60 to 0.55 (Sonnet at low effort instead of medium); `quality` keeps `routing.auto` off, raises the demand to 0.90 (Opus at medium effort for ordinary requests) and stops using the low (Haiku) tier. Escalations, risk and failure handling, pins, an explicit effort, hard policy and required safety are unchanged, `routing.subscription` is never touched, and while a mode other than `balanced` is set every candidate must be an exact Claude catalog model the organisation's managed model policy allows (an unreadable policy leaves nothing eligible, so the request is forwarded unchanged). Stored in `routing/mode.json`. See Routing.

items.summary: `taksim budget enforce --mode downgrade`: opt-in budget enforcement, off by default.
items.details: While a developer or repo budget window is at or above its threshold (`--at`, `--daily-at`, `--monthly-at`, percent of the limit, default 100), the gateway serves routed Claude requests on a cheaper tier (`--to sonnet`, the default, or `haiku`) instead of only warning. It never blocks a request or leaves Claude, forwards the original request on any routing error (and retries once on the requested model after an upstream failure before the first byte), skips explicit pins, required-safety requests and phases that already escalated, applies the organisation's model policy to the target, and is released when the day or month rolls over, the limit is raised or enforcement is turned off. Every step down is a routing decision with evidence source `budget_downgrade` and `BUDGET_DOWNGRADE` reason codes plus a `ROUTING_DOWNGRADE_OBSERVED` event; `taksim budget status`, `diagnostics downgrades` and `report weekly` count them and the status line shows `, sonnet cap` in sessions the gateway can cap. A step down the `/advisor` guard would undo is skipped (`BUDGET_DOWNGRADE_SKIPPED:ADVISOR_GUARD`). Settings live in the `enforcement` block of `budgets.json`. See Routing.

items.summary: Claude `/advisor` support: the gateway forwards the advisor tool, its beta header and the advisor response blocks and usage unchanged, and no longer swaps the executor model into a pairing the API would refuse (or past encrypted advice or a paused advisor call); it keeps the client's model and records `advisorRoutingSkipped` with the reason.
items.details: Advisor tokens, reported only in `usage.iterations`, are now recorded as their own execution per advisor model in the gateway and the Claude transcript import, priced at the advisor model's rates, shown in `taksim report task-cost`, and kept out of downgrade counterfactuals. The pairing check follows the API's model compatibility list. An advisor result without reported advisor usage, or an advisor model without a known price, is flagged as not priced instead of counted as zero. See `docs/ROUTING.md`.

items.summary: Updater: `taksim update --apply` on Windows now checks the downloaded `install.ps1` against the release's `SHA256SUMS.txt`, as macOS already did, and refuses on a mismatch or a missing entry.
items.details: A build that is not signed (every release so far) no longer accepts a bootstrap with a valid signature from an arbitrary publisher: a signed bootstrap must come from a publisher pinned in the binary (none yet), and an unsigned one still needs `--allow-unsigned`. A signed build compares the signer's issuer as well as its subject. Consequence: builds released before the publisher is pinned cannot recognise the first signed release, so `taksim update --apply` refuses it (with or without `--allow-unsigned`). Install that release once with the one-line installer from the README; later signed updates go through `taksim update --apply` again.

items.summary: Installers: `install.ps1` applies the same rule to `install-release.ps1`, and `install-release.ps1` to `taksim.exe`.
items.details: When no signed Taksim is installed, a signed file must come from a publisher in the script's pinned list, which must match the updater's list (a test checks this). A signed install needs the same subject and issuer, or a pinned signer. A duplicate `SHA256SUMS.txt` entry is now refused, and entry names are matched case-sensitively.

items.summary: macOS home migration safety.
items.details: `taksim home migrate` takes its lock before it scans for other Taksim processes, scans again under the lock, and no longer deletes `-wal`/`-shm` itself: after it checkpoints and closes its own connection, a sidecar that is still there means another process has the database open (even idle), and the migration stops with exit 3 before anything moves. With taksim.dev's files in `~/.taksim`, generic names (`cache`, `logs`, `reports`, `team`, `policy`, `routing`, `gateway`, `vendor-*`) are left alone by `uninstall --purge-data` and move with `home migrate` only when named with `--include`, marker or not. During an interrupted migration only `status-line` and the fail-open hooks (including desktop routing's `desktop-register`/`-unregister`/`-liveness`) exit 0 silently; `taksim doctor` names the generic entries a plain rerun leaves behind and the `--include` they need; every other command, also with stdin redirected, exits 3 with a one-line message. `install.sh` treats exit 3 from `home path --create` as a warning, so `taksim update --apply` still completes and hands off the gateway. `macos.yml` has a manual `home-tests-only` input that runs only the `TaksimHome` tests.

items.summary: CI cost: GitHub Actions no longer runs on every push to `main`; `ci.yml` runs its Linux check weekly and on manual dispatch.
items.details: `release.yml` runs only on `v*` tags and only when the repository variable `TAKSIM_ACTIONS_RELEASE` is `true` (releases are built locally), skips the integration and performance tests on the hosted Windows runner (new `ci-local.ps1 -SkipIntegrationTests`; the local merge gate still runs them), has a 30-minute timeout, and starts the macOS jobs only after Windows passes. `macos.yml` cancels the other architecture when one fails and runs the unit tests on Apple Silicon only.

items.summary: macOS: the default Taksim home moves to `~/Library/Application Support/EdgeeTech/Taksim`, out of the `~/.taksim` that taksim.dev also uses and its Homebrew zap deletes.
items.details: `TAKSIM_HOME` still wins; Windows (`%USERPROFILE%\.taksim`) and Linux (`~/.taksim`) are unchanged. An existing `~/.taksim` with Taksim's marker or Taksim data stays in use, and `taksim doctor` warns with `TAKSIM_HOME_LEGACY_LOCATION`; one shared with taksim.dev stays in use too, with a warning, until `taksim home migrate --shared`. New `taksim home migrate [--dry-run] [--shared] [--include NAME]` moves only Taksim's own entries under an exclusive lock and a journal. It checkpoints the databases first (`BEGIN EXCLUSIVE`, `wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE)`) so each moves as one file, refuses links, stages entries next to the new home (renamed on one volume, copied and verified across volumes) and publishes them last, rolling back on failure. An interrupted migration makes Taksim commands refuse (hooks and the status line skip silently) until a rerun resumes it, and doctor reports `TAKSIM_HOME_MIGRATION_IN_PROGRESS`. A new home whose database holds data is never overwritten. It leaves foreign files and a `TAKSIM-HOME-MOVED.txt` breadcrumb, removes `~/.taksim` only when empty, and refuses while a gateway, another Taksim process or desktop routing is active. New `taksim home path [--create]` prints the home; the macOS installer uses it to create the new home (`0700`) for new installs. `uninstall --purge-data` accepts the new home. Rolling back to a binary older than 0.3.16 after migrating needs `TAKSIM_HOME` set to the new path.

items.summary: Data safety: Taksim no longer risks deleting another product's data in a shared home. taksim.dev, an unrelated macOS app, also uses `~/.taksim` and `TAKSIM_HOME`.
items.details: Taksim now writes an ownership marker (`.edgeetech-taksim`, schema version and install id) into its home and backfills it at startup when the home holds Taksim files and none of taksim.dev's. `taksim uninstall --purge-data` purges only a home with the marker, or with Taksim files and no taksim.dev files, and otherwise refuses. It deletes only Taksim's own entries and removes the directory only when it is empty afterwards, on Windows and macOS. `taksim doctor` warns with `TAKSIM_HOME_SHARED_WITH_FOREIGN_PRODUCT` (or `TAKSIM_HOME_UNKNOWN_FILES`) and a `homeNote`, and on macOS recommends `taksim home migrate`.

items.summary: Docs: README now shows v0.3.15, the unsigned `-AllowUnsigned` install and a capability summary.
items.details: ROUTING, CLIENTS, PRIVACY_AND_COMPLIANCE and MACOS no longer describe the Claude desktop app Code tab as routable or subscription sessions as never routed.

items.summary: Release hardening.
items.details: The published package no longer carries the XML documentation files (about 1.4 MB of member descriptions) or PDBs: `Directory.Build.props` sets `PublishDocumentationFile=false`, `PublishReferencesDocumentationFiles=false` and drops every `.pdb` from the publish set, while build output keeps both for the analyzers, debugging and tests. `scripts/Test-ReleaseArtifact.ps1` now fails when a published directory or the release zip holds an `.xml`, `.pdb` or `.dbg` file, or when the single-file bundle manifest lists one. `taksim.exe` version info now shows `Copyright © 2026 EdgeeTech Ltd. All rights reserved.` The local release builder moved into the repository as `scripts/release/Build-LocalRelease.ps1` (website checkout is a parameter or `TAKSIM_WEBSITE_ROOT`, restore is locked, and it applies the same publish settings); `docs/DEVELOPMENT.md` documents the steps. Installs made before this change keep their `.xml` files until `taksim install cleanup` removes the old version directory.

items.summary: Legal: EULA version 1.1, effective 22 October 2026.
items.details: Governing law and courts are now England and Wales, with consumer protections kept. New restrictions: no use of Taksim to build a competing product; no extraction or redistribution of embedded prompts, rubrics, policies, pricing and model catalogs or calibration data; no circumvention of licence checks or plan limits. A new confidentiality section covers non-public materials. The reverse-engineering restriction now names the exceptions in sections 50A-50C and 296A of the Copyright, Designs and Patents Act 1988, which it does not override. The licence names the Free, Pro and Team plans, and the privacy section lists the only services Taksim connects to.

items.summary: Pricing: the official OpenAI price refresh reads the new standard price table.
items.details: OpenAI reordered the columns and replaced the single cache-write column with 30-minute and 12-hour cache-write columns, so the refresh was rejected. The parser now maps columns by header name, keeps the 30m and 12h write rates under `30m` and `12h` for both context bands, and still reads the old single `cache writes` layout. An unknown, duplicated or missing column, a half-present cache-write pair or an unparseable price still fails the refresh and keeps the last good catalog. Rows labelled `(<272K context length)` were skipped silently before. They hold both bands in one row, so they now import into the existing `standard_short` and `standard_long` tiers. The catalog has no field for the numeric threshold, so it is not stored: a consumer must pick the band itself. The legacy list-price lookup does not read OpenAI catalog bands, and it no longer stops at an OpenAI model that the catalog holds: an official refresh used to leave such a model (for example `gpt-5.4`) unpriced in reports, and the verified built-in rate now prices it below and above the 272K threshold. A model with no built-in rate, such as `gpt-5.5`, stays unpriced until an override sets one. A priced row with a label the parser cannot read now fails the refresh instead of being skipped.

items.summary: Pricing: follow-ups to effective-dated prices.
points: `pricing-overrides.json` schema 3 lets one model hold several dated windows. Windows that overlap, are partly undated or disagree on `preferOverride` are rejected at load with a reason. An execution in a gap between windows is left unpriced, never priced at zero.

An optional `timeZone` (`UTC`, a UTC offset or an IANA id) normalises a window to UTC when it is read, so a boundary-day execution is priced instead of left unpriced. Only the UTC hour holding a bound that is not on a whole hour (a `UTC+05:30` midnight, say) stays unpriced.

The official Anthropic and OpenAI price sources emit dated schedules from a trailing `(through ...)` or `(from ...)` qualifier on a model row. Private fabric prices accept `validFrom`, `validUntil` and `timeZone`.

Schema 1 and 2 override files, catalog snapshots and frozen task contracts load, serialize and price exactly as before. Saving the overrides file keeps entries that failed to load instead of dropping them.

items.summary: `taksim doctor` no longer leaves the `unknown` Claude credential state unexplained.
items.details: Doctor still does not run `claude auth status` unless given `--probe-claude-auth`, so a saved `/login` stays `unknown` (`saved_login_unclassified`) there while `taksim claude credentials` probes and reports `subscription` for a claude.ai login. `claudeCredentialNote` now says the probe was skipped and names `taksim doctor --probe-claude-auth` and `taksim claude credentials` as the ways to classify. With the flag, doctor matches the launcher.

items.summary: NativeAOT groundwork: JSON goes through source-generated serializer contexts.
items.details: The trim/AOT analyzer pass now reports 87 warnings instead of 797; the JSON-reflection share fell from 766 to 56. Serialized output, stored metadata, digests and CLI `--json` output are byte-for-byte unchanged: a parity test compares every generated type with the reflection serializer under every options set the product uses, and a golden test pins payloads that were anonymous objects, and gateway golden tests pin the execution-record metadata, `/health`, routing status and the hook replies (ASP.NET's relaxed encoder included). The 56 left are the non-generic enum converters (12), `Dictionary<string, object>` metadata (14), OTLP telemetry payloads (12), the public generic signing helpers of the native evidence bridge (8), judge request bodies with open-ended members (6), the Cursor hook fragment (2) and one reflection `--json` helper (2). `scripts/aot/Test-JsonReflectionWarnings.ps1` (opt-in `ci-local.ps1 -AotJsonBudget`) fails on any warning not in its baseline file. Release binaries are unchanged and are still not NativeAOT.

items.summary: Security: the local gateway is hardened against misuse by other software and web pages on the same machine.
points: The client's request path is appended to the provider base URL and can no longer select a different upstream host, scheme or port. Such a path gets HTTP 400 `invalid_upstream_path` and nothing is sent upstream. Paths with an encoded slash (`%2F`) or any other percent-escape left after decoding (for example a double-encoded `%252F`) are refused too. This also refuses Bedrock- or Vertex-style encoded ARN model ids, which are not supported upstreams today.

The provider endpoints and `/dashboard` now apply the loopback `Host` check that `/health` already had (HTTP 421 otherwise), and refuse browser requests from other sites with HTTP 403. CLI clients are not affected. `/dashboard` sends the same security headers as `taksim dashboard`. Each refusal names its reason in `x-taksim-error` (`misdirected_host`, `cross_site_request`, `invalid_upstream_path`) and a small JSON error body.
Provider redirects are passed back to the client and never followed; the upstream client keeps no cookies and has a 30 s connect timeout.
Browser-only request headers (`Cookie`, `Origin`, `Referer`, `Sec-Fetch-*`, `Sec-CH-*`) are no longer forwarded upstream. All other headers still are.
The Anthropic, OpenAI and Gemini upstream base URLs share one check: an absolute `http` or `https` URL, any host.
Gateway client adapters must now state their credential policy explicitly; there is no permissive default.

items.summary: Internal: event-type storage names now come from `CanonicalEventStorage` instead of repeated literals (stored values unchanged), with a guard test; ARCHITECTURE.md describes the Domain layer accurately; renamed the unit `CostAttributionTests` class.
Internal: Edge no longer touches EF Core or `TaksimDbContext`.
items.details: The execution recorder, downgrade outcome recorder, judgement count cache and managed session lifecycle moved to Infrastructure; the routing decision writes, routing snapshot reads, performance samples and the `routing`, `routing outcome`, `pricing`, `report cost` and `diagnostics downgrades` queries are Infrastructure adapters. `IDowngradeOutcomeSink` and `CanonicalExecutionObservation` are Application contracts; `IInferenceExecutionSink` sits with the recorder in Infrastructure. Behaviour, SQL, diagnostics and CLI output are unchanged; a new architecture test keeps EF Core, the context and raw SQLite out of Edge. The Connector's hook handler now names `SESSION_STARTED` through `CanonicalEventStorage`.

items.summary: Internal: the shadow policy file loader and the Taksim home resolution moved from Application to Infrastructure; Application keeps the pure shadow policy parser and an `IShadowPolicySource` port, and a guard test keeps file and environment access out of Application.
items.details: Same environment variables, defaults and precedence.

items.summary: Internal: `GatewayPipeline` takes one `GatewayPipelineOptions` record instead of 19 constructor parameters, with the same defaults.
items.details: `TaskEvidenceCollector`, `ClaudeHistoricalImportService` and the public offline calibration artifact generator are split into collaborator classes by responsibility (storage, report building, evaluator import, record mapping, row writes, validation, prior and findings). Public APIs, evidence, imports and generated artifacts are unchanged. A guard test fails when a `src` file outside migrations and generated code exceeds 1,000 lines.

items.summary: Internal: catch-all blocks that swallowed their exception were reviewed.
items.details: Three are narrowed to the expected exception types. Ten now print a `TAKSIM_INTERNAL_DEGRADED` line on stderr with the exception type only: decision memory reuse, fingerprinting, learning and lessons (`DECISION_MEMORY_*`), a failed judge batch (`JUDGE_BATCH_FAILED`), evidence tier recalculation (`EVIDENCE_TIER_RECALCULATION_FAILED`) and lost judge or router service-call observations (`JUDGE_SERVICE_CALL_OBSERVATION_FAILED`, `ROUTER_SERVICE_CALL_OBSERVATION_FAILED`). The gateway reports a stale decision-memory hint snapshot once per failure streak (`DECISION_MEMORY_HINTS_STALE`), and an unreadable fingerprint key (`DECISION_MEMORY_FINGERPRINT_FAILED`) or a failing decision engine (`DECISION_ENGINE_FAILED`) once per process, never per request. `taksim notify status` shows `unavailable` for an enabled channel whose settings or stored credential cannot be read, instead of `not configured`. The rest stay silent with a `// Best-effort:` comment that says why. A guard test fails when a `src` catch-all neither rethrows, records a diagnostic, uses the caught exception nor carries that comment.

items.summary: `taksim update --apply` now runs exactly the installer bytes it verified.
items.details: On Windows the download is written to a new file in a fresh private temp directory. That file is reopened read-only and write-denied (a Windows sharing mode) for verification and the installer's lifetime, and re-hashed against the downloaded bytes; any difference stops the update. Its Authenticode signature is then checked, and that same held copy runs. The directory is removed on every path. On macOS the download is checked against `SHA256SUMS.txt` in memory and handed to bash as its command string, so no file exists to swap. The `--allow-unsigned` behaviour and the macOS checksum source are unchanged.

items.summary: The CodeBuddy, Gemini CLI, Kimi Code and Qwen Code history importers now run on the shared importer base like the other clients.
items.details: Run records, skip-unchanged checks, source and session rows and error handling come from one place, so a fix to the shared pipeline reaches them too. Imported rows and results are unchanged. One difference: an unexpected error in one of these imports now ends the run as failed and is rethrown, instead of leaving the run marked running. Resource discovery after the import is unchanged: still run for CodeBuddy, still not run for the other three.

items.summary: Secret files under TAKSIM_HOME are now created atomically and owner-only.
items.details: The hook secret, the installation salts (`installation-salt`, `cache/installation.salt`) and `decision-memory.key` are written to a private temp file and published with a no-overwrite move. Before, the launcher and the gateway could both create the hook secret on first run and disagree, and a crash mid-write left a corrupt secret. On Unix new files are 0600 from creation, and an existing file with a wider mode is tightened to 0600 on first read. Windows keeps the TAKSIM_HOME user-profile ACLs. File names and contents are unchanged, so existing installs keep their values. An empty or truncated file left by a crashed older writer is replaced in place under an exclusive handle, so concurrent first runs still agree. Sharing violations from antivirus or the indexer are retried for about 2 s before startup fails with a clear timeout. Known limit: on a mixed-version first run, where an older binary and a new one create the secret at the same moment, they can still disagree once. Restarting fixes it.

items.summary: `taksim claude` no longer promotes a status line from a project `.claude/settings.json` or `.claude/settings.local.json` into its `--settings`.
items.details: That would run a project-sourced command without Claude Code's workspace-trust prompt. Every directory from the launch directory up to the git root is checked. When one of these files defines a status line, or cannot be parsed, Claude's native precedence applies and the Taksim status stays in the terminal title. A user-level status line is still composed with the Taksim status, as before. A config directory inside the project chain (for example `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=<workspace>/.claude`) counts as user settings. `--setting-sources` is now recognised (it was misspelled `--settings-sources`): without `user` the user status line is not composed, and without `project` or `local` those files are ignored.

items.summary: Internal: event-type storage names now come from `CanonicalEventStorage` instead of repeated literals (stored values unchanged), with a guard test; ARCHITECTURE.md describes the Domain layer accurately; renamed the unit `CostAttributionTests` class.

Internal: the shadow policy file loader and the Taksim home resolution moved from Application to Infrastructure; Application keeps the pure shadow policy parser and an `IShadowPolicySource` port, and a guard test keeps file and environment access out of Application.
items.details: Same environment variables, defaults and precedence.

items.summary: Raw benchmark NDJSON moved out of `docs/`.
items.details: The ten `docs/performance-*.ndjson` files (about 5.7 MB) are now assets of the `perf-data-2026-10` release; `docs/PERFORMANCE.md` links to them and the JSON reports and tables stay in the tree. No test, script or CI gate read them. The benchmark command regenerates them under the gitignored `artifacts/`.

items.summary: Build hygiene.
items.details: NuGet lock files (`packages.lock.json`) are now committed for every project and CI, the release build and `scripts/ci-local.ps1` restore with `--locked-mode`, so a dependency cannot change without a reviewed lock-file diff. The lock files cover the publish runtimes (`win-x64`, `osx-arm64`, `osx-x64`); publish steps now use `--no-restore` after the locked restore. NuGet audit is explicit (`NuGetAudit`, `NuGetAuditMode=all`, so transitive packages are checked) and NU1901-NU1904 are errors. `ci-local.ps1` gains a "Vulnerable packages" step (`dotnet list package --vulnerable --include-transitive`) that fails on any finding or when the audit cannot run. `.wrangler/` and `.claude/` are git-ignored.

items.summary: Fixed-configuration task runs through the gateway can now be verified evidence.
items.details: Before, a `taksim claude --model` run had no routing decision, so no execution had an applied configuration and every context-benchmark report was a mixed treatment. For a request it forwards with the client's original bytes, the gateway now records the model, effort, thinking mode and budget, context variant and whether any typed (server) tool was declared, never content. On a run registered with one treatment and propensity 1, `task collect` uses those tokens as the applied configuration (`canonical-gateway-observed-fixed`) and verifies the run assignment as the phase authority. A call on another model, effort or thinking mode still makes the episode mixed and unverified. Subscription calls (`claude_subscription_gateway`) get an API-equivalent amount at the first-party list price; when no server tool was offered, server-tool fees are zero instead of unknown. Quota-unit amounts stay unknown: there is no measured quota source. Outcomes still need `import-evaluation` from an independent evaluator; `evaluate-local` stays diagnostic only. Bytes may differ only through the arm's declared context strategy, which must keep the observed tokens. Only Anthropic Messages bodies are read. The observed thinking version is `request-observed-v1`, so a fixed plan must use it.

items.summary: Connectivity probes and token counts are no longer inference evidence.
items.details: The gateway stops recording non-POST requests (Claude Code's `HEAD /api/hello` startup probe, `GET /v1/models`) and the free `/count_tokens` and `/responses/input_tokens` endpoints as executions, so they no longer block `task begin` or reach `task collect` and gate 9. One-token quota probes are billed and stay recorded.

items.summary: `taksim claude`, `codex` and `devin` adopt `TAKSIM_PREREGISTERED_SESSION_ID`, so `task begin` can register the session before launch.
items.details: An unusable or already used id refuses the launch, a registered session never falls back to native, and the variable is not passed to the child.

items.summary: Sessions routed by `taksim desktop on` show which model served.
items.details: The per-prompt liveness probe now sends Claude's session id and the gateway can answer with a one-line hook `systemMessage`. This applies to plain `claude` terminal and VS Code sessions; Claude desktop app Code-tab sessions are not routed (next entry), and the desktop app shows such messages only behind a server-side feature gate. On the first prompt of a registered session: "Taksim manages this session: …". After that, only when the served model changes: "Taksim: previous reply was served by Sonnet 5.5 (requested Opus 5.5)." and "Taksim: back to Opus 5.5 after your correction." Only main-conversation turns count (not subagents or side requests). The notice carries model names only. A probe still takes about 0.16 s. Run `taksim desktop on` again to install the new probe; the 0.3.13 probe keeps working without notices.

items.summary: Desktop routing reports when it cannot reach a session.
items.details: The Claude desktop app (2.42304, Claude Code 2.1.299) starts Claude Code with `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=https://api.anthropic.com` in its launch environment, and Claude Code prefers a launch-environment value over the settings `env`, so a real desktop session sends every request directly to Anthropic: the gateway sees none and Taksim records no session. The SessionStart hook now compares the session's effective base URL with the settings value, records the endpoint (scheme and host only) on the session entry, and shows a notice; `taksim desktop status` lists such sessions and warns.

items.summary: `taksim.exe` now carries the Taksim icon and version info (file description `Taksim`, product `Taksim`, company `EdgeeTech`), so Windows Task Manager shows the logo and name.
